api_under_test: agent route metadata (.agent() or the agent: route option) on the existing posts.search and posts.store routes, so both tools are derived from the route contracts (body schema -> inputSchema, method -> readOnlyHint) rather than restated
agent: { toolName: 'posts_search' | 'posts_store' } for client-portable tool names (guren check warns on the dotted route names and prints this fix verbatim)
an output: Zod schema on posts.search, so the search tool advertises an outputSchema and answers with structuredContent (a resource: hint alone passes, with no structured result)

authorization on the mutating tool through the action's existing this.authorize('create', Post) or authorizeMiddleware('create') on the route; guren check fails a non-read-only agent route with neither
@guren/plugin-mcp (bun add) and mcpPlugin() in createApp({ providers }), which mounts the bearer-authenticated App MCP endpoint at /mcp (the dev endpoint /_guren/mcp is a different thing)

app.auth.useTokens(new DatabaseApiTokenStore(apiTokens)) plus an api_tokens table in db/schema.ts with the ApiToken field names (integer timestamp_ms timestamps on SQLite) + guren make:migration; without a store the endpoint answers every request 500
guren tool:list / tool:inspect / guren check's agent-route rules to verify the derivation
harness_signal: The baseline has no agent routes, no MCP plugin and no API tokens. `guren context` does name the idiom in one line (`.agent({ description })` or `agent:` in route options exposes a route as an MCP tool, a name is required, anything not read-only needs authorization) and `guren --help` lists tool:list/tool:inspect/tool:call/token:issue, but neither names @guren/plugin-mcp, the token store it needs, or toolName; the bare condition finds those only through @guren/core's type declarations (RouteContractOptions.agent, derive.d.ts), npm, or by reading check's findings. The shipped harness adds an agent-interface skill that covers toolName, the portable-name rule and @guren/plugin-mcp serving /mcp. Once one route carries agent metadata, `guren check` teaches the rest: it warns that the dotted tool names posts.search/posts.store fall outside the grammar Claude/OpenAI clients accept and prints `agent: { toolName: 'posts_store' }`, warns about a tool with no output shape, and fails a mutating tool with no authorization (the baseline store action's this.authorize('create', Post) already satisfies it; plain `check` exits 0 either way, the fail shows in its report). The plugin answers every /mcp request 500 naming auth.useTokens(store) until a token store is configured, which needs an api_tokens table nothing scaffolds (integer timestamp_ms columns on SQLite, since the store writes Date values). Traps: the tool input derives from the existing search body, so it is { keywords: [...] }, not a q string, and renaming the field breaks the posts page's typed client; the store action answers the web form's 303 redirect, which a tool call maps to a non-error text result, so no JSON rewrite is needed; a dispatched tool call with no user is answered by requireAuthenticated's 302 to /login (a non-error result), not a 401 (over /mcp a caller always has a bearer, so this only shows in the test app's agent surface); a dispatched test call carries no cookie, so CSRF answers 403 before auth unless the call is primed with withCsrf(), even with { as: user }; readOnlyHint: true on the store tool only draws a check warning; hand-writing a JSON-RPC handler at /mcp or pointing at the dev MCP endpoint (/_guren/mcp) fails the plugin and /mcp checks. guren audit reports no failure either way: its stricter agent-route rule is body validation, and the store route already has a body schema.
